scenarios.title: The Group Chat Roasts {J}
text: The old school group chat has found a clip of {J}'s worst touch of the season and set it to circus music. It has been playing on loop for an hour. {BFf} has made it the group photo.
The group chat has a new name: '{J} Can't Defend'. It's had the name for three days. Nobody has changed it back.

choices.label: Roast them back, harder
choices.text: He posts a photo of {BFf} at fourteen with a haircut that should be illegal. The chat explodes. Balance is restored.

choices.label: Leave the chat in mock protest
choices.hint: They'll add you back in 30 seconds.
choices.text: He leaves. Twenty-eight seconds later he's added back with a new nickname, which is worse.

choices.label: Mute it, you're busy
choices.text: He mutes it. When he checks later, the joke has moved on without him. That stings more than the joke.

scenarios.title: An Old Friend Turns Sour
text: A friend from the youth team, who didn't make it, posts a long message online: '{J} forgot where he came from.' He hasn't spoken to {J} in a year. Neither of them called the other.
At a home visit, an old friend makes a joke about {J} 'being too good for us now'. The table laughs. The joke had teeth.

out.text: The call is awkward for five minutes and honest for an hour. He admits he's struggling. They meet next time {J} is home.
He doesn't pick up. He posts a screenshot of the missed call with a laughing emoji.

choices.label: Ignore it publicly, hurt privately
choices.text: He says nothing. The post fades. The feeling doesn't.

choices.label: Reply in public
choices.text: His reply is fair, but it's public. The argument becomes a story in {OUT}. Mutual friends pick sides.

scenarios.title: {BFf} Is Getting Married
text: {BFf} calls, voice shaking: he's getting married, and he wants {J} as his best man. The wedding is in three months. It falls on a matchday.
{BFf} proposed! The wedding date is set. He wants {J} to give the best man's speech. He has also, accidentally, chosen the day of a cup tie.
scenarios.prompt: The date clashes with a match.

ok.text: {Mf} sighs and says, 'Family is family. Go.' The speech makes the whole room cry, including {BFf}'s father, who has never cried.

bad.text: {Mf} says no. {J} records his speech on video. It's played on a projector. {BFf} says he understands. He doesn't, fully.

choices.label: Skip the match, go anyway
choices.hint: Your friend will never forget it. Nor will the club.
choices.text: He goes. The best day of {BFf}'s life. The club fines him two weeks' wages and {Mf} doesn't look at him for a month.

choices.label: Ask him to move the date
choices.text: There's a silence on the phone. 'The venue's booked, bro.' He finds another best man. They're still friends. Different friends.

scenarios.title: The Entourage Grows
text: Somehow there are seven people in {J}'s apartment who weren't there last month. Cousins of friends. Friends of cousins. One of them is wearing {J}'s jacket.
{J}'s new 'friends' are always available, always fun, and always looking at the bill when it arrives.

choices.label: Clear the house
choices.hint: Quieter life. Some will badmouth you.
choices.text: He keeps three people and asks the rest to leave. One of them sells a 'story' to a gossip account a week later. It's mostly lies.

choices.label: Keep the party going
choices.text: The parties are legendary. The bills are too. {BFf} comes once, looks around, and leaves early.

choices.label: Ask {BFf} who's real
choices.hint: Trust the person who knew you before.
choices.text: {BFf} looks at the list and crosses out five names without hesitating. He's right about all five.

scenarios.title: {T} Invites {J} Home
text: {T} invites {J} for dinner with his family. His wife cooks, his kids climb on {J} like a tree, and nobody mentions football for three hours.
{T} has a spare ticket to a concert on Saturday. 'It's not your music,' he says. 'Come anyway.'

choices.label: Go and stay late
choices.hint: A real friend in the squad.
choices.text: It's the best evening he's had in this city. {T} drives him home at midnight. Something has changed between them.

choices.label: Go, but leave early
choices.text: He's a good guest for two hours and leaves before dessert. {T} says 'next time, stay'.

choices.label: Make an excuse
choices.text: 'Next time,' says {J}. {T} nods. Next time doesn't come.

scenarios.title: {BFf} Has Been Arrested
text: A call at 2am from {BFf}'s brother: {BFf} has been arrested after a fight outside {PLACE}. He says he was defending someone. He needs a lawyer and doesn't have money for one.
{BFf} is in a police cell. A misunderstanding, he swears. The bail is more than he earns in a year.

choices.label: Pay for a lawyer quietly
choices.hint: Loyalty. If the press finds out...

out.text: The lawyer gets him out by morning. The charges are dropped. {BFf} doesn't know how to thank him, so he just hugs him for a long time.
It works — but a journalist finds out who paid. 'Footballer bails out brawling friend' runs in {OUT}.

choices.label: Go to the station in person
choices.text: He sits in the station waiting room all night. A photo of him there is everywhere by breakfast. {BFf} will never forget it. Neither will the club.

choices.label: Send money, stay away
choices.text: He sends the money through {BFf}'s brother. It helps. {BFf} notices that {J} didn't call.

scenarios.title: A Friend in a Foreign City
text: At the gym near his apartment, a local guy his age keeps spotting {J} on the bench press. He doesn't seem to care about football at all. That's what makes him interesting.
The barista at the café near training always writes {J}'s name wrong on purpose. Today she's written 'the new guy who looks lost'. He laughs. She invites him to a quiz night.

choices.label: Say yes to everything
choices.text: Quiz nights, cheap dinners, a birthday party where nobody asks for selfies. Slowly, the city stops feeling foreign.

choices.label: Keep to yourself
choices.text: He keeps it professional. The apartment stays quiet. Some nights, too quiet.

scenarios.title: A Forgotten Birthday
text: {BFf}'s birthday was yesterday. {J} remembers at 11pm today, scrolling past photos of a party he wasn't at and a cake that says '{BFf} 🎉'.
The group chat is full of birthday messages for {BFf}. They're from yesterday. {J}'s isn't one of them.

choices.label: Call and grovel
choices.text: {BFf} lets it ring four times on purpose before picking up. Then he laughs. 'You owe me {FOOD}. A lot of it.'

choices.label: Send an outrageous gift
choices.text: The gift is so ridiculous that {BFf} posts it everywhere. All is forgiven. Mostly because of the gift.

choices.label: Pretend you were busy
choices.text: 'Busy with work.' {BFf} replies: 'Yeah.' Just that.

scenarios.title: The Charity Match Back Home
text: The old neighbourhood is organising a charity match: {J}'s childhood friends against a team of local celebrities. The proceeds go to the clinic where {J} was born.
{BFf} has organised a charity game back home and put {J}'s name on the poster before asking. The tickets have sold out.

out.text: He plays for the old team, scores twice, and lets the local mayor score a penalty. The clinic gets a new wing.
A local celebrity, a singer who has never played, scythes him down in the first minute. Small knock. Huge photos.

choices.label: Come and coach from the sideline
choices.text: He shouts instructions like a real manager. His friends lose 5-1 and blame his tactics.

choices.label: Ask them to take your name off
choices.hint: Sensible. Feels like betrayal back home.
choices.text: The poster is reprinted without his name. Ticket refunds are requested. The neighbourhood remembers.

scenarios.title: The Online Rivalry
text: {BFf} has beaten {J} at the football video game eleven times in a row and is posting the results. Fans have found the posts. They're taking sides.
A friend from home challenges {J} to a live-streamed game. Loser has to wear the other's club shirt for a day.

out.text: He wins in the last minute. Thirty thousand people watch live. {BFf} demands a rematch on air.
He loses 6-0. He wears his friend's local team shirt to training. The squad photograph it from every angle.

choices.label: Play privately
choices.text: They play until 2am, trash-talking like they're twelve. Nobody else sees. That's the point.

scenarios.title: A Friend's Business Idea
text: {BFf} wants to open a small futsal centre in the old neighbourhood and name it after {J}. He needs an investor. He also needs {J}'s face on the sign.
An old friend pitches {J} a clothing brand. The designs are actually good. He wants a partner, not a sponsor.

choices.label: Invest and be involved
choices.hint: Could flourish. Could fail. Either way, you're in it together.

out.text: It works. Within a year it's a local institution. Kids who can't afford academies play there for free on Sundays.
It struggles, then closes. The money's gone. The friendship survives, just about.

choices.label: Lend your name only
choices.text: His name on the sign brings customers. {BFf} is grateful, a little disappointed.

choices.label: Decline
choices.text: {BFf} says he understands. He finds another investor. The sign has someone else's name.

scenarios.title: The School Reunion
text: A school reunion. Everyone wants a selfie. Nobody asks how he is. The girl he had a crush on at fourteen is there, married, and lovely, and asks only about his salary.
The reunion is in the old school hall, which seems smaller than he remembers. A teacher who said he'd 'never amount to anything' is now telling everyone she 'always believed in him'.

choices.label: Be gracious to everyone
choices.text: He signs, smiles and listens for four hours. Driving home, he feels empty and full at the same time.

choices.label: Find your real friends in a corner
choices.text: He finds the four people who always mattered and they talk in the car park until midnight. Nothing has changed. Everything has.

choices.label: Remind the teacher
choices.text: 'You said I'd never amount to anything.' The table goes silent. It feels good for exactly ten seconds.

scenarios.title: {T} Needs a Place to Stay
text: {T} has split up with his girlfriend and has nowhere to live. He asks if he can stay on {J}'s sofa 'for a week'. Weeks are flexible in football.
{T}'s flat has flooded. He turns up with a suitcase and a hopeful face.

choices.label: Yes, as long as he needs
choices.text: The week becomes six. He leaves dishes everywhere and the apartment has never been livelier. They become inseparable.

choices.label: One week, strict
choices.text: One week, a list of rules on the fridge. {T} breaks all of them and leaves on day seven with a thank-you card.

choices.label: Help him find a hotel
choices.text: He books {T} a hotel and pays the first night. {T} is grateful. Slightly less close.

scenarios.title: Tickets, Tickets, Tickets
text: Every friend he's ever had wants tickets for the big game. The club gives him four. He has received thirty-one requests, including from a man he met once at a bus stop.
The derby is coming and {J}'s phone has become a ticket office.

choices.label: Family and {BFf} only
choices.text: His family and {BFf} sit together in the stand. Twenty-seven other people quietly mute him.

choices.label: Buy extra tickets for everyone
choices.text: He buys a block of seats for {cost}. Thirty people in his name. They make a banner. It's misspelled.

choices.label: Raffle them in the group chat
choices.text: The raffle becomes a three-day saga with accusations of rigging. It's the most fun the group chat has had in years.

scenarios.title: Something's Wrong With {BFf}
text: {BFf}'s messages have become strange: short, flat, sent at 4am. When {J} calls, he says he's 'just tired'. He's been just tired for a month.
{BFf}'s sister messages {J}: 'Have you spoken to him? He's not himself. He won't talk to us.'

choices.label: Go home and see him
choices.hint: Costs time and a training day.
choices.text: He flies home on his day off. They sit on the old wall behind the school until 3am. {BFf} finally talks. Then he agrees to see someone. It's a start.

choices.label: Call every day
choices.text: Ten minutes every evening, no matter what. Slowly, the calls get longer. Slowly, {BFf} laughs again.

choices.label: Send him a message and hope
choices.desc: He'll reach out if he needs to.
choices.text: 'Here if you need me.' He doesn't reply. {J} tells himself that means he's fine.

scenarios.title: The Friends Video
text: {BFf} posts a video of {J} losing at a street game of keepy-uppy to an eleven-year-old. It's going viral. {J}'s agent has called twice.
A video of {J} and the old crew singing badly in a car goes viral. In the background you can see the club's training ground. And a very illegal U-turn.

choices.label: Repost it, laughing
choices.text: He reposts it with 'I want a rematch'. The kid gets invited to the club's academy open day. {BFf} becomes briefly famous and unbearable.

choices.label: Ask {BFf} to delete it
choices.text: {BFf} deletes it, slowly, with a voice note that says only: 'Got it, boss.'

scenarios.title: The Friends You Left Behind
text: Looking through old photos, {J} realises he hasn't spoken properly to anyone from home in months. The group chat has moved on. His friends' lives have new names in them.
{BFf}'s new girlfriend, new job, new apartment — {J} learned about all three from social media.

choices.label: Schedule a weekly call
choices.text: Sunday calls start awkward and become essential. By the third week, it's like he never left.

choices.label: Fly them all out for a weekend
choices.text: Five friends, one weekend, a city none of them have seen. They watch him play. They cry when he scores, then deny it.

choices.label: Accept that life moves on
choices.text: He accepts it. Friendships have seasons. This one might be ending.

scenarios.title: A 'Friend' Sells a Story
text: {OUT} runs an 'exclusive' from 'a lifelong friend' of {J}: stories about his childhood, his family's money troubles, and a girlfriend from school. Half of it is true. That's the worst part.
A gossip account posts screenshots from a private group chat. Someone in {J}'s old circle has sold him out.

choices.label: Find out who, cut them off
choices.text: It takes a day to figure out. He removes one person from his life. The group chat goes silent, then slowly recovers.

choices.label: Make a public statement
choices.text: His statement is dignified. It also means the story runs for another three days.

ok.text: {JR} writes a sympathetic piece about friendship and fame. The public sides with {J}.

bad.text: {JR} runs it, but the headline makes it look like a feud. More fuel on the fire.

scenarios.title: Keeping a Promise
text: {J} promised his first coach a visit. The old man is in a small house near the pitch where it all started, a blanket on his knees and every newspaper clipping of {J}'s career on the wall.
The visit he promised. The old coach's daughter opens the door and starts crying before he's said a word.

choices.label: All afternoon
choices.hint: Some debts are paid in time.
choices.text: They watch an old tape of a youth match on a VCR. The coach points out every mistake {J} made at eleven. They laugh until they cry.

choices.label: An hour, with photos
choices.text: The photos of them together go everywhere. The coach's phone rings for a week with old players calling him.

scenarios.title: The Kid From the Street
text: The boy {J} spotted playing in sandals is now in an academy. He's sent a video: a goal from a youth match, a celebration copying {J}'s, and a message: 'One day I'll play against you.'

choices.label: Become his mentor
choices.text: Monthly calls. New boots every season. The boy calls him 'coach', which is ridiculous and perfect.

choices.label: Send a signed shirt and a voice note
choices.text: The boy pins the shirt above his bed. The voice note is his phone's alarm sound for a year.
